name: Scopa Bazzica
description: Two-player Scopa variant from Italy in which players capture table cards by matching value or sum, score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera, plus optional Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind) declared after each three-card deal. First to 21 or 31 points wins.

overview.description: Two-player Scopa variant from Italy in which players capture table cards by matching value or sum, score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera, plus optional Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind) declared after each three-card deal. First to 21 or 31 points wins.

history.origins: Scopa is one of Italy's major card games, with roots in Naples and possible links to Spanish games such as Primero. Bazzica is a traditional two-player Scopa variant in which players score extra points by declaring three-card combinations (Bazzica or Bazzicotto) after each deal; it is documented as part of Italian card-game tradition.
timeline: Traditional: Regional Scopa variant (Bazzica) documented in Italian card-game traditions.

setup.players: Two players only. Scopa Bazzica is designed for head-to-head play with no partnership or team option.
setup.deck: Standard 40-card Italian deck (coins, cups, swords, batons; King 10, Horse/Queen 9, Jack 8, 7-2 face value, Ace 1).
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; opponent cuts. Deal one card at a time until each player has three cards; place the next four cards face up on the table. If three or four Kings appear in the table layout, redeal. After each round of three cards played, deal three more to each player (no new table cards). Repeat until deck is empty.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table by matching value or sum; score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, primiera, and for declared Bazzica (3 pts) or Bazzicotto (10 pts). First to 21 or 31 points wins.
rules.gameplay: Two players. Deal three cards each and four face up on the table. Non-dealer plays first. Each turn play one card: capture a single table card of equal value, or a set of table cards whose values sum to the played card, or leave the card on the table. Capture is compulsory when possible; if both a single card and a set match, take the single card. Clearing the table is a scopa (1 point). After each three-card deal segment, before playing, players may declare Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind); only the better declaration scores. After all three cards are played, dealer deals three more to each player; repeat until deck empty. Last captor takes remaining table cards. Score the hand; deal passes; play until one player reaches 21 or 31.

scoring.description: Points for each scopa (1), most cards (1), most coins/diamonds (1), settebello (1), best primiera (1), plus Bazzica (3) or Bazzicotto (10) when declared. First to 21 or 31 wins.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach agreed target (21 or 31 points) wins the game.
